title: Constrain insight pipeline to essential dashboard/tracing/cost modes for Q2 launch
creator: Aisha Khalid
description:
Goal: Ship a focused, high-value console surface for the Q2 public launch by trimming non-critical dashboard and tracing features and deferring complex cost breakdowns. We need a predictable, performant experience that covers engineering and platform teams' most common use cases while limiting scope to what we can deliver within the release window. This ticket documents the scope cuts, tradeoffs, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the trimmed surface.

Scope changes summary:
- Keep: route-level and model-level cost summaries, per-route latency histograms (90th & median), top-3 cost drivers card, single-click drilldown into raw logs/dashboard.
- Remove (defer to post-launch): token-level waterfall charts, per-request KV cache heatmaps, full flamegraph trace visualizer, multi-dimension cost cohort explorer, advanced attribution linking to billing exports.
- Reduce: tracing detail to sampled traces (1% default sample) with summarized span timing and error hotspots instead of full span-by-span interactive flamegraphs.
- UX change: Replace multi-card heavy landing screen with a single compact “Console Snapshot” card (summary knobs: most-costly routes, top error classes, latency tail) and a lightweight inspector panel that opens on demand.

Why these cuts:
- Engineering: Granular token timelines and full flamegraphs require kernel-level instrumentation and additional backend index work that would push delivery beyond the Q2 window.
- Product: Early users prioritize quick signal about cost spikes, latency regressions, and major errors. A summarized view provides high signal-to-noise for most customers.
- Cost & Reliability: Reducing sampling and deferring heavy aggregation avoids production load increases on the new telemetry pipeline during launch.

Tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Tradeoff: Losing token-level timelines reduces root-cause fidelity for model quality regressions. Mitigation: Provide a documented escalation path and an on-demand debug mode (opt-in for customers with Dedicated capacity) that enables deep traces post-launch.
- Tradeoff: Lower trace sampling means some outlier behaviors may be missed. Mitigation: Add transient higher-rate captures tied to anomaly detection (post-launch) and maintain a lightweight error stack snapshot for every failed request.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for release):
1) Console Snapshot card loads in under 1.2s on 95% of internal test accounts across regions, using staging telemetry.
2) Top-3 cost drivers card correctly surfaces route, model, and instance class with values matching billing exports within a 5% delta for sampled daily aggregates.
3) Latency histograms (p50/p90) render for selected route within 1.5s and match production telemetry within 10% on a synthetic 24h workload.
4) Sampled trace detail shows span summary and 95th tail latency, and sample rate is configurable per-customer in the console (default 1%).
5) When telemetry ingestion falls below SLA (data lag > 2 minutes), console displays an explicit degraded state and a link to the ingestion status page.
6) Removed features are gated behind a clear “Deep Diagnostics” roadmap banner with instructions for customers to request early access.
7) No customer-facing error pages introduced by the trimmed surface; all missing features route to fallback UI with docs links.

Review notes & feedback log:
- 2025-03-11 (Engineering): ENG feedback requests deferral of KV cache visuals; they estimate 3 weeks of infra work to safely index prefixes. Decision: defer.
- 2025-03-12 (Design): DES recommended a greyscale-first palette and single-card focus to avoid cognitive load; recommended language for roadmap banner. Design will supply final pixel mocks by 2025-03-19.
- 2025-03-14 (Security): No immediate elevation; KMS integration not required for trimmed surface.
- 2025-03-16 (Telemetry team): Proposed default trace sample rate at 0.5% to reduce ingestion risk. PM decided to keep 1% default but expose config in settings.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0 (internal alpha): Ship to internal accounts and SRE + select solutions engineers for 1 week smoke.
- Week 1 (closed beta): Enable for 10 pilot customers (opt-in) with a short survey and Slack channel for feedback.
- Week 2 (open beta opt-in): Gradually expand to all trial accounts but keep advanced deep diagnostics off by default.
- Week 4 (GA): Flip to default for public launch after triage of pilot feedback and final perf checks.

Next steps (owners assigned):
- ENG: Implement summary aggregation queries and route-level cost APIs (ENG-19876). Due 2025-03-24.
- DES: Finalize compact snapshot card and provide Figma specs (DES-2201). Due 2025-03-19.
- PM: Finalize acceptance test harness, coordinate pilot customers, update PRD with deferred feature list. Due 2025-03-18.

Notes for handover to release engineering:
- Ensure feature flag gating for all deferred items. Flag names: feature.console.deep_diagnostics (default: off), feature.console.trace_sample_rate_override.
- Provide a rollback plan: disable snapshot polling and serve static placeholder until root cause resolved.
